evidence: Pinned comments identify empty/truncated and HTTP 200 HTML checksum inputs; README, QUICKSTART, and release docs say integrity-only output does not verify authenticity.
adoption.rationale: The source-pinned preflight requires one well-formed SHA256 record before calling the platform checksum command; the contract isolates this guard from authenticity and downstream checksum semantics.

contract.declared_domain: One ASCII LF-delimited checksum or error-response line, excluding NUL. The solver property covers every line of length 0..63. The guarantee covers checksum-record preflight only and does not establish authenticity or model the external checksum utility.
contract.guarantee: When a downloaded SHA256SUMS file has no line beginning with exactly 64 ASCII hexadecimal digits followed by POSIX whitespace, an optional `*` marker, and a non-whitespace filename character, verify-release.sh fails before calling the platform checksum command and cannot print an integrity success result. This is a preflight guarantee only; it does not establish release authenticity.
contract.input_source: The SHA256SUMS text file accompanying a downloaded release artifact; it remains untrusted network input until signature verification succeeds. The helper documents integrity-only operation while the maintainer signing key is unavailable.

domain: ASCII single SHA256SUMS line of length 0..63
